hypothesis: The ring A bridge truncates native stats OOB packets at the text NUL; a guarded binary-length path should deliver the whole upload to the local game server without changing the successful connect path.

baseline.qualification: The same-option r833 control did not emit a stats packet; r832 demonstrates the truncation but also had a separate diagnostic b command. This is a transport-path comparison, not a claim about stats emission frequency.

guarded_change: tools/ring_bridge_1649370.py --preserve-binary-stats uses the native [chunk:u8, wireLength:u16] header after the text NUL to bound packet length to 13 + min(1238, remaining bytes). The default NUL path remains unchanged. tools/session_up_1649370.py forwards the opt-in flag.

after.r834_bridge: raw stats prefix has nul=9, forwarded len=1002, source=stats164_header
after.r835_bridge: all four native stats packets have nul=9, forwarded len=1000, source=stats164_header

source_boundary: The local game server currently splits the OOB text at the first NUL and on_stats() sends statResponse <challenge> without parsing the binary payload. Community same-Build CODOL_AcceptClientStats164() documents 1238-byte chunks, optional zlib, 32768-byte profile, and missing-mask acknowledgement. Thus full packet delivery is verified but profile assembly, client-slot binding, ESC loadout, and normal match state are not.
cleanup: Only the existing r107flow runtime was used. r833/r834/r835 experiment client, game-server and bridge processes ended or were stopped by their verified exact PIDs. The live SQLite SHA-256 remained 06F7A93BC8F818461FC0267F464BB3FA0E3801AC999462FC54EB8CC512AF2F70; integrity_check=ok. No profile bytes were added to tracked evidence.
